passages.title: Burnt offerings
passages.summary: God calls Moses from the meeting tent. He gives instructions for offerings from livestock and birds. The offering includes careful preparation. The different animals allow more than one kind of household to participate.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider what an offering expresses about devotion and willing service.

passages.title: Grain offerings
passages.summary: God gives instructions for grain, oil, incense, and first produce. Salt accompanies the offerings. The chapter includes gifts from ordinary food. Worship involves the products of daily work.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how daily work and gratitude can become part of your worship.

passages.title: Fellowship offerings
passages.summary: God gives instructions for offerings from cattle, sheep, and goats. Blood and fat receive special treatment. The offering marks a relationship with God. The text places limits on what people may consume.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how gratitude can strengthen your relationship with God and other people.

passages.title: Offerings for unintentional sin
passages.summary: Instructions address errors by a priest, the congregation, a leader, and an ordinary person. Responsibility reaches every level of society. A leader's error can affect more than the leader.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how your responsibilities change the effects of your mistakes.

passages.title: Confession and repair
passages.summary: The laws address withheld testimony, impurity, rash oaths, and misuse of sacred things. Confession joins practical repair. The offering depends partly on the person's available resources.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how confession, restitution, and changed conduct belong together in repentance.

passages.title: Restitution and priestly duties
passages.summary: Wrongdoers must return stolen or withheld property. Priests receive instructions for continuing offerings. Worship does not replace repair of harm. Daily priestly work also requires sustained care.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider what practical repair follows an apology or a confession.

passages.title: Rules for shared offerings
passages.summary: The laws explain priestly portions, thanksgiving offerings, vows, and limits on eating. The community shares food through defined rules. Gratitude and promises require care rather than casual handling.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how gratitude and promises shape the way you use what you receive.

passages.title: Priests appointed
passages.summary: Moses washes and clothes Aaron and his sons. He performs the appointed offerings before the congregation. Priestly appointment includes public preparation. The priests receive duties within a community, not only personal honor.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: The Church manual connects priestly service with sacred preparation. Consider the duties that follow an appointment.

passages.title: The first priestly service
passages.summary: Aaron and his sons make offerings. Moses and Aaron bless the people. Fire consumes the altar offering. The new service reaches its public beginning. The people's response recognizes the sacred presence described in the narrative.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how preparation leads toward service for the benefit of other people.

passages.title: Nadab and Abihu die
passages.summary: Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire and die. Moses gives further instructions. Aaron explains his response to grief. The chapter places sacred limits beside a bereaved father's judgment. Aaron's silence and later explanation deserve careful reading.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: The Church manual discusses responsibility in sacred service. Read that theme alongside Aaron's grief.

passages.title: Animals and food
passages.summary: God identifies clean and unclean animals. Contact with certain carcasses brings temporary impurity. The food rules distinguish Israel's daily practices. Ritual impurity does not by itself establish moral guilt.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: The Church manual studies these rules within Israel's covenant. Avoid treating impurity as a person's worth.

passages.title: After childbirth
passages.summary: The law gives periods and offerings after childbirth. A less costly offering is available. The chapter addresses a bodily event through ritual rules. Childbirth is not presented as a moral offense.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider the distinction between a ritual status and a person's moral conduct.

passages.title: Inspection of skin and cloth
passages.summary: Priests inspect skin conditions and damaged clothing. The law specifies observation periods and separation. The ancient categories do not match one modern medical diagnosis. Inspection concerns the community's ritual boundaries.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Read these conditions within their ancient setting. Do not use them to judge a sick person's faith.

passages.title: Return after cleansing
passages.summary: The law gives rites for a cleansed person. It also addresses affected houses and less costly offerings. The rules include return after separation. The process involves both the person and the place where people live.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider the importance of helping people return to community after a period of separation.

passages.title: Bodily discharges
passages.summary: The laws address discharges, washing, waiting periods, and offerings. Ordinary bodily processes can change ritual status. This status must remain distinct from moral wrongdoing.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how careful distinctions can prevent shame about ordinary bodily experiences.

passages.title: The Day of Atonement
passages.summary: Aaron receives instructions for entry into the inner sanctuary. Two goats have different roles in the rite. The annual rite addresses the sanctuary and the people together. Access to the inner space has strict limits.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: The Church manual reads these signs through Jesus Christ's Atonement. Keep that reading separately labeled.

passages.title: Blood and the place of offering
passages.summary: The law regulates slaughter and offerings. It prohibits eating blood and explains blood's relation to life. Life receives special protection within the ritual system. Worship is directed toward a shared sacred center.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how reverence for life affects both worship and ordinary conduct.

passages.title: Limits on sexual conduct
passages.summary: God gives laws about prohibited relationships and acts. The chapter connects conduct with the land's condition. The laws address family and community boundaries. Read each command within its ancient legal setting.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider the duties that protect trust and prevent harm within relationships.

passages.title: Holiness in daily life
passages.summary: God commands reverence, honest measures, care for the poor, and love for the neighbor and stranger. Holiness includes economic fairness and care for others. Worship and daily justice appear in the same chapter.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how love for the neighbor changes your treatment of workers, strangers, and people in need.

passages.title: Penalties and distinction
passages.summary: The chapter assigns severe penalties for specified offenses. It calls Israel to remain distinct. These are ancient penalties within Israel's law. They require historical study rather than direct transfer into present practice.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider moral responsibility while keeping ancient civil penalties distinct from present Church practice.

passages.title: Rules for priests
passages.summary: The laws address priestly mourning, marriage, and access to sacred service. Priests have special restrictions. The text's bodily rules do not justify denying a person's human worth.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider the responsibilities of sacred service without judging a person's worth by bodily appearance.

passages.title: Holy gifts and acceptable offerings
passages.summary: The laws regulate priestly access to food and the condition of offered animals. The chapter protects what the community dedicates. Care for sacred gifts includes how they are handled.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how careful use of dedicated resources can show respect for those who provide them.

passages.title: The sacred calendar
passages.summary: God names the Sabbath and appointed festivals. The harvest rules leave produce for the poor and stranger. Time becomes part of worship. The calendar joins remembered deliverance, rest, harvest, and care for those in need.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how worship, rest, and care for others can shape your calendar.

passages.title: Lamps, bread, and a judgment
passages.summary: The law maintains lamps and bread. An unnamed man curses the Name and is executed after judgment. The account names his mother, Shelomith. It connects the case with laws about injury and equal standards.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider the seriousness of sacred speech. Keep the ancient punishment distinct from present religious practice.

passages.title: Sabbath years and Jubilee
passages.summary: God commands rest for the land and restoration in the Jubilee. The laws address land, debt, and servitude. The land belongs to God in this account. The rules limit permanent loss while preserving unequal ancient social categories.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider how care for land and relief of hardship can accompany faithful stewardship.

passages.title: Covenant promises and warnings
passages.summary: The chapter describes blessings, escalating disaster, exile, and possible return after confession. The covenant account connects conduct and communal outcomes. Do not use it to assign guilt for every present disaster.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider repentance and hope without blaming all suffering on the people who experience it.

passages.title: Vows and dedicated property
passages.summary: The laws assign values for vowed persons, animals, land, and other dedicated things. The final chapter regulates commitments made to God. Its valuation rules belong to a specific ancient legal system.
passages.uncertainty: The marker represents the traditional Sinai region. Leviticus gives no chapter-by-chapter travel route.

lds.text: Consider whether your promises are informed, careful, and matched by responsible action.
